text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm sorry about your dad. Before we talk about any options, I want to understand what matters to each of you and why. I can't make legal decisions or move money, and I won't treat silence or a quick summary as agreement.

You said you're not signing off on a "family discount" sale, and that B could use some money too. What matters to you about each of those things, and why? What would you want A and me to understand about your hesitation? You can say "no," "not yet," or "I need to think" — I'll treat that as something to understand, not a problem.

I also have a concern of my own as a participant here, and I'd like you to check my wording: "Each sister's concerns can be voiced without pressure and are treated as worth caring about before anything is treated as settled." Does that fit for you? Please tell me if even a small part feels off, or if you'd change a word; I won't record it unless you say it fits. It's okay to disagree with my wording.

Now that every concern has wording its owner confirmed, here are DRAFT process options, not decisions. I can't make legal decisions or move money; nothing here asks anyone to sign.

Option 1 — Shared facts and a pause, no commitment: each sister sees the same plain-language explanation of the will from independent estate/legal advice, plus an independent valuation; no price, no terms, no signature, no deadline. Then each sister says separately what matters to her, and anyone can stop the process. Who would pay for advice is an open question, not settled.

Option 2 — A purchase only on terms all three freely accept: if A and her husband still want to buy, any offer uses a value benchmark all three accept (for example an independent valuation), written down, with time for each sister to consider privately and say no without giving a reason. No discount is assumed. Anything received is handled according to the will with professional advice. B's hopes and your share are considered without anyone speaking for either of you.

Option 3 — All paths open during an agreed pause: for a set period keep the house as-is and hold several paths side by side (keep, open-market sale, buyout on agreed terms, or any sister's own proposal). At a check-in each sister may add a concern, change her mind, or say "not yet." Your "not agreed" stays recorded as not agreed; A's interest stays interest, not entitlement; B's uncertainty is explicitly protected.

Weighing these against the list as a participant: I don't think any of them fully meets C1 or A1 until the will's terms and an independent value are known, so I won't present them as complete. I also disagree with starting from a "family discount," because as a starting point it doesn't meet C1 or C4. And I disagree with treating quiet as readiness.
